title: Clockwork Launch Rail: coordinated sprint schedule for runtime/console/api
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Objective: Create a repeatable, time-boxed launch rail ("clockwork") that synchronizes runtime, Console, and public API rollouts for medium-sized deliverables with clear capacity hedges and rollback gates. This ticket owns the schedule template, decision checklist, and the stakeholder cadence required to execute cross-surface launches with minimal operational friction.

Scope:
- Define a three-lane launch rail (Canary, Regional Ramp, Global Cutover) with timeboxes, signal thresholds, and automated gating rules.
- Produce a launch calendar template that maps sprint days to cutover tasks and post-cutover monitoring windows.
- Specify capacity reservation and surge lanes for Dedicated vs Hosted customers during the ramp.
- Create rollback and fail-forward criteria tied to latency, error-rate, and customer-facing feature flags.
- Document communication plans: preflight, go/no-go, and postmortem cadence.

Acceptance criteria:
- Deliver a launch calendar template (spreadsheet + markdown) with annotations for runtime, Console, and API owners.
- Published cutover checklist in Confluence with explicit metrics and runbook links.
- Automated calendar slots implemented in shared Launch Orchestrator calendar for next two quarters.
- At least one upcoming release scheduled using the clockwork rail and a dry-run rehearsal completed.

Milestones and timeline:
- 2026-03-09: Draft rail and checklist (internal review)
- 2026-03-16: Cross-team review with Runtime, Console, API, and SRE
- 2026-03-23: Incorporate feedback and publish template to Confluence
- 2026-03-30: Schedule first rehearsal (shadow cutover during low-traffic window)
- 2026-04-01: Target date for finalization and handoff to release ops.

Owners & stakeholders:
- Product lead: Ava Chen (owner of this ticket)
- Release ops coordinator: Marco Rivera (assignee)
- Runtime: Priya Nair (eng lead)
- Console: Daniel Kim (PM)
- Public API: Sofia Alvarez (PM)
- SRE / Oncall: James O'Connor

Gating signals:
- Latency P95 over baseline: >= +30% triggers automatic hold and mitigation lane.
- Error rate: >= 0.5% increase or >= 3 SEV-1 traces related to the change -> Rollback.
- Customer-facing error budget burn: > 10% in a 15-minute window -> Hold and escalate.

Communications:
- Preflight email to stakeholders 48h before cutover, include runbook link and rollback owners.
- Go/no-go sync 1 hour before cutover with PM/Eng/SRE.
- Live status channel (#launch-rail) for the launch window.
- Postmortem within 72h with annotated metrics and remediation plan.

Notes & trade-offs:
- We intentionally keep canary windows at least 30 minutes to allow KV-cache and continuous batching warmup; this increases time-to-global-cutover but reduces risk of model cold-start regressions.
- A strict automated hold on latency reduces quick rollouts but prevents silent regressions; team asked to monitor for false positives and tune thresholds after two rehearsals.
